t109: Do I need an Emirati partner to set up my company?
t110: No, in most cases. In a free zone, a company can be 100% foreign-owned, and since 2021 this has also been possible on the mainland for most activities. A few regulated activities remain subject to specific conditions.
t112: There is no personal income tax. Companies in principle pay 9% corporate tax on the portion of profit above AED 375,000, with a 0% rate possible for some free zone companies on their qualifying income, and 5% VAT. Your situation in your home country matters too: we discuss it from the first conversation.
t113: How long does it take to get set up?
t114: It depends on the project. A free zone company can be set up in a few days or a few weeks once the file is complete; the bank account and visas often take several more weeks. For a family, it's best to start 4 to 6 months before your arrival date, especially for housing and visas.
t115: Do you also handle real estate and the management of my property?
t116: Yes: search, purchase, then letting and management of your property, with the Cevitas Real Estate team, a RERA-licensed agency (ORN 49294). And if you move here, the same team takes care of the rest: company, visas, family, university studies.
t117: Do you also help with university studies?
t118: Yes. For a student who wants to study in Dubai or elsewhere in the UAE: choosing the programme and the university, the application, student visa, housing and settling in, with their parents at every step.
